A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original intent/topic classification experiments, ASR measurements, and manual transcription evaluation, including Tables 2–4 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments comparing cascaded classifiers trained on gold text versus ASR transcripts in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The text-only, speech-only, and cascaded architectures, classification components, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Appendix E varies the source of training text as an experimental control, without introducing a new algorithmic component or objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same German/Bavarian intent-classification data from MASSIVE, Speech-MASSIVE, and xSID, and German/Swiss German topic-classification data from SwissDial. The additional control uses transcripts of existing training utterances; it adds no task, population, or evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: The classifier, speech-model, ASR-model, and simple-baseline membership is unchanged in the retained comparisons. Appendix E uses existing mBERT/mDeBERTa combinations with XLS-R 300M DE, Whisper tiny, and Whisper large-v3 to vary training-text preparation.

E3.justification: v1 trains cascaded classifiers on gold German text. v2 additionally trains six intent-classification configurations on transcripts produced by the same ASR model used at evaluation. This adds a focused training-source control; the original splits, metrics, and experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix E tests whether training on ASR transcripts changes the conclusions about cascaded systems, with paired comparisons in Tables 10–11. Appendix F.2 adds three paired German/Bavarian transcription case studies in Table 12. Existing sensitivity and manual ASR analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed means and standard deviations, together with the same ASR dispersion and correlation significance reporting. The new control follows the existing three-seed practice; no increase in repetitions or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 10–11 add control results with mixed effects. On Bavarian xSID, ASR-trained mBERT/XLS-R 300M DE scores 51.8%, versus 57.5% for its retained gold-trained counterpart; mDeBERTa/Whisper tiny scores 39.6%, versus 30.3%. These are different training conditions. All original tabulated scores are retained, and Table 12 adds qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: The empirical measures and accuracy-difference definitions are retained. Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory findings, and conclusion retain the same claims about differing modality preferences for standard German and dialects, the usefulness of ASR normalization, and the dialectal audio intent dataset. The additional control supplies support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the mixed ASR-training effects through training noise and differences in transcription errors across splits. It expands limitations concerning dataset requirements, instruction-tuned model comparisons, and unverifiable speech-pretraining exposure, replacing the previously untested cascade-training concern with qualified empirical evidence.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the six control configurations and their matched ASR preprocessing, and newly discloses that speech-model pretraining datasets are not openly accessible. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, recording specifications, resource links, and promises of future code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Faruqui and Hakkani-Tür on ASR–NLU integration and four works supporting encoder-based classification: Adelani, Ojo, Kasa, and Saattrup Nielsen and colleagues. These provide focused methodological positioning; the broader related-work account remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 tightens abstract/introduction wording, corrects typos, expands the model-selection explanation, and introduces labeled limitations paragraphs. It inserts Appendix E and reorganizes the existing ASR and detailed-results appendices, while retaining the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds two control-result tables and a color-coded transcription-example table. Original Tables 10–11 become Tables 13–14; Table 1 moves and Tables 3–4 share a page. Figure 1 and the established table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly leaves the possible disadvantage of gold-trained cascades untested. v2 partially addresses this weakness through six ASR-trained controls in Appendix E, finding mixed accuracy changes but broadly retained modality trends. Concrete transcription examples and clearer model limitations improve interpretability. The restricted control subset and unresolved pretraining exposure keep the overall gain limited.
